newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide ad spend seen growing over next 4 years.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide ad spend seen growing over next 4 years.

text.p: Worldwide spending on advertising is expected to grow in the next four years and major media advertising will slightly increase its share of global economic spending, according to forecasts published on Wednesday by media specialists Zenith Media.
Zenith, the media planning and buying unit of British advertising and marketing group Cordiant Plc, said it expects to see advertising expenditure driven by real economic growth in many markets.
Major media advertising spending is forecast to account for 1.02 percent of world economic spending in 1996 and is seen rising to 1.03 percent in 1999, Zenith said.

In the U.S. television is expected to be the most successful medium in the next four years and will receive an extra boost in 1998 from the winter Olympics. Magazines will benefit from the stricter regulation of tobacco and alcohol advertising on TV.

Media spending in 1996 in Europe was worth $77 billion -- $1 billion more than Zenith forecasted six months ago. The German media market is being propelled by rising competition and greater market transparency.

The UK, by contrast, is expected to grow more slowly as it is "caught between the pincers of rising consumer inflation and the expected arrival of the first left-wing government in 18 years," Zenith said. "However, it should return to form in 1998."

Britain is widely expected to elect a Labour government in its next general election, which much be called by May 22 at the latest. Conservative Prime Minister John Major has said that he will call an election by May 1, although the Tories' recent loss of its parliamentary majority has raised speculation that an election may be held earlier.
In Asia growth comes mainly from Japan, representing 60 percent of Asia-Pacific advertising spend. Japan's 1996 ad spend accelerated well ahead of economic growth.

The second wave "tigers" are expected to materially increase their share of emerging Asian ad spend between now and 1999. China and India together presently account for 20 percent of the market (excluding Japan and Australia). Both China and India are growing by between 20 per cent and 25 per cent a year, Zenith said.
In China domestic advertisers are driving demand and they are being helped by better TV and print research.
In India the cable TV industry is presenting a formidable alternative to the state TV monopoly.
These two markets are expected to be 30 percent of the Southeast Asian total by 1999.
The Philippines and Indonesia currently account for eight percent of the emerging regional ad spend. By 1999 this is expected to double to 16 percent.

Zenith said it remains optimistic about the prospects for advertising in Latin America. "Most of the region's economies are on the right track with easing inflation and rising growth, and in future years will depend more on advertising to drive consumption" said the report.

Most Latin American advertising markets have grown at or above expectations, only Brazil has been a disappointment. But Zenith said "with ad spend growth falling to a low of 10 per cent in 1997 before picking up again, the Brazilian ad market remains in good shape."

Growth in Venezuela is the most precarious in Latin America. "Instead of the expected decline in Venezuela we have seen real expansion fuelled by high income from oil exports. This growth will however, be highly sensitive to oil prices" Zenith said.
